source.title: Large Learning Rates Simultaneously Achieve Robustness to Spurious Correlations and Compressibility
source.authors: Melih Barsbey; Lucas Prieto; Stefanos P. Zafeiriou; Tolga Birdal

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and supplementary material; no apparent cutoff or garbling affecting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests learning-rate effects on training outcomes related to V1 in CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but focuses on generalization, spurious-feature use, and compressibility rather than training classification error. It does not report the training-error comparisons required by V1.
record.gate_note: The text states that models are trained to 100% training accuracy, but does not give separate CIFAR-10/100 training-error results by learning rate. CIFAR figure results concern test accuracy, prunability, representation statistics, and feature attributions, so they do not directly test V1's training-error claim. Other cited findings are prior work, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses training to 100% accuracy as a convergence criterion for comparing generalization and compressibility. It does not separately report achieved CIFAR training errors. Its large-learning-rate results do not measure a stability threshold or curvature dynamics, so they do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that high learning rates jointly promote robustness to spurious correlations, network compressibility, and favorable representation properties in their tested settings. They propose confident mispredictions of bias-conflicting samples as an explanatory mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Studies learning-rate effects on spurious-correlation robustness and compressibility, not the training-error outcomes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects are examined across datasets, architectures, learning rates, and training schemes; the CIFAR-10/100 section reports qualitative attribution differences between low- and high-learning-rate models.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher learning rates improve robustness to spurious correlations, compressibility, and several representation measures across the tested datasets and architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate influences generalization, compressibility, and reliance on spurious features.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors associate large learning rates with confident mispredictions of bias-conflicting samples and disruptive gradient updates, drawing an analogy to catapults. They do not measure curvature or locate a stability threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large learning rates can implicitly reweight training toward bias-conflicting examples and reduce reliance on spurious features.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The CIFAR-10/100 attribution comparison is qualitative; the text does not provide numerical training-error outcomes by learning rate. Figures normalize some axes, and the authors direct readers to supplementary material for value ranges.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: CIFAR-10/100 results concern test accuracy, compressibility, attribution, and representation statistics rather than training classification error. Other training-error statements are not reported as separate results for these datasets and learning-rate conditions.

untested.parts: Achieved training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, and its dependence on model size, regularization, and training duration. Section 4.2 specifies a stopping criterion rather than reporting these outcomes.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on excess student width.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special initialization, or normalization.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to uses_without_test/T4. Figure 25 explicitly discusses attained convergence, but concerns Colored MNIST, outside V1's named datasets. CIFAR attribution and test-performance results do not establish training error. Learning-rate-specific training-error comparisons are not inherently required to support V1; the issue here is that the CIFAR statement specifies the training procedure rather than separately reporting attainment.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 across learning rates, model sizes, label corruption, and training duration.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU local minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error as depth increases, and the cited special cases involving initialization or normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth.
Training dynamics and stability when learning rates exceed a stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
